title: Cohomological dimension of the base field
statement:
If $K$ is an algebraically closed field, then $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)=0$. If
$K$ is a finite field, then $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)\leq1$.

proof.text: Let $K$ be a field, choose a separable closure inside an algebraic closure $\Omega$, and put $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K^{\rm sep}/K)$. By [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules], geometric stalks give an additive equivalence $E$ from all abelian étale sheaves to discrete $G$-modules. With $L=K$, [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants] identifies sections naturally with $E(F)^G$; the germ maps preserve addition. Here is the formal derived comparison explicitly: an additive equivalence and its inverse preserve kernels and cokernels by their universal properties, hence preserve exact complexes; the identification of Hom groups with those under the inverse equivalence preserves the defining acyclicity condition for K-injective complexes. Thus, if $F\to I^\bullet$ is the resolution used in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], then $E(F)\to E(I^\bullet)$ is a K-injective resolution of $E(F)$, and the two complexes obtained by sections and invariants are termwise naturally isomorphic. Part (1) of [det-base-field-cd-cochains] identifies the latter derived invariants with continuous-cochain cohomology. Consequently $H^s(K_{\Et},F)\cong H^s(G,E(F))$ for every $s\geq0$, with no finite coefficient ring or uniform annihilator assumption.

source.place: Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point; Tag 04JM, lemma-global-sections-point; Tag 03QU, lemma-compare-cohomology-point; continuous cochains as in the cited blueprint lemma

proof.text: Suppose $K$ is algebraically closed. It is separably closed, so [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives vanishing for every torsion étale sheaf in positive degrees. Apply part (4) of [det-cd-etale-comparison] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $c=0$ to obtain $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)\leq0$. The spectrum of a field is affine, hence qcqs; instantiate the auxiliary qcqs morphism in that comparison as $g=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$.

source.place: first paragraph, algebraically closed case; sk-def-cd/sk-def-cd-etale-comparison.md, part (4)

proof.text: For the reverse inequality, take the trivial discrete $G$-module $A=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z\neq0$ and its inverse image $F$ under [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules]. Additivity and faithfulness show $\ell\,\mathrm{id}_F=0$, since $\ell\,\mathrm{id}_A=0$; therefore $F$ is an $\ell$-power torsion sheaf. The section formula of [lem-exc-field-sections-stalk-invariants] with $L=K$ gives $H^0(K_{\Et},F)=A^G=A\neq0$. Part (2) of [det-cd-etale-comparison] then puts degree zero in the supremum defining $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)$, so the upper bound from step 2 is equality. This argument works also when $\ell=\operatorname{char}K$.

source.place: Consequences, last paragraph: nonzero degree-zero sheaf; explicit inverse-equivalence construction

proof.text: Now let $K$ be finite. By [det-base-field-cd-galois-group], its absolute Galois group is isomorphic as a profinite group to $\widehat{\mathbf Z}=\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, with transition maps given by reduction when the indices divide. We may compute continuous cohomology on this group: pull back the action and each continuous cochain along the topological group isomorphism. The cochain differential uses only the group product and action, so this pullback commutes with the differential and has inverse given by the inverse isomorphism. By part (1) of [det-base-field-cd-cochains], it also identifies the cohomology groups.

Let $M$ be any torsion discrete $\widehat{\mathbf Z}$-module. For $x\in M$, its open stabilizer contains the kernel of projection to some finite cyclic quotient, since a basic neighbourhood of the identity restricts finitely many coordinates and their least common multiple dominates them. Its orbit is therefore an image of this finite cyclic quotient and is finite. If $ex=0$, every element of the orbit is killed by $e$; the subgroup generated by an orbit of size $t$ is a quotient of $(\mathbf Z/e\mathbf Z)^t$, hence finite and stable. For a finite list of elements take the sum of their finite stable subgroups, which is finite as an image of their finite product. These subgroups, ordered by inclusion, form a small nonempty directed partially ordered set: they are a subset of the power set of $M$, contain the zero subgroup, and the sum contains any given pair. Their union equals $M$. Part (2) of [det-base-field-cd-cochains] gives $H^s(\widehat{\mathbf Z},M)=\varinjlim_A H^s(\widehat{\mathbf Z},A)$ over its finite stable submodules $A$. It therefore suffices to prove vanishing in degrees $s\geq2$ for finite $A$.

Let $A$ be a finite discrete $\widehat{\mathbf Z}$-module and choose $e\geq1$ with $eA=0$ (take $e=1$ if $A=0$). The intersection of the open stabilizers of its finitely many elements is an open action kernel. From the inverse-limit topology, this kernel contains the kernel of $\widehat{\mathbf Z}\to C_m=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$ for some $m\geq1$: a basic neighbourhood restricts finitely many coordinates, and their least common multiple gives such an $m$. Every projection to $C_n$ is surjective: a residue represented by an integer $a$ is the image of the compatible family of residues of $a$ in all cyclic quotients. Thus $\widehat{\mathbf Z}/K_n\cong C_n$ for its coordinate kernel $K_n$, and the action factors through $C_m$. The projections to $C_n$ with $m\mid n$ still present $\widehat{\mathbf Z}$ as an inverse limit: any finite list of coordinates is dominated by an index divisible both by $m$ and all those indices. Their kernels all act trivially on $A$. They are cofinal, under reverse inclusion, among all open normal subgroups acting trivially on $A$: for any such subgroup $N$, the same finite-coordinate argument gives a coordinate kernel $K_d\subseteq N$, and $K_{\operatorname{lcm}(m,d)}\subseteq K_d\subseteq N$. Thus the inverse-limit hypothesis in part (3) holds over the whole family as well. Restricting its colimit to these coordinate kernels changes no classes or equalities: each representative at $N$ inflates to one of them, and any equality witnessed at another subgroup inflates to a common multiple of its coordinate index and the finitely many indices already in use. Part (3) of [det-base-field-cd-cochains] therefore gives $H^s(\widehat{\mathbf Z},A)=\varinjlim_{m\mid n}H^s(C_n,A)$ along inflation.

source.place: Finite modules, action kernel and cyclic quotient colimit

proof.text: Fix $s\geq2$. For every index $n$ divisible by $m$, apply only the final clause of [det-base-field-cd-inflation] to $C_{en}\to C_n$, with $r=e$ and module $A$. Its hypotheses hold because $eA=0$, so the inflation $H^s(C_n,A)\to H^s(C_{en},A)$ is zero. Every element of the colimit in step 6 has a representative at one index $n$ and becomes zero at $en$; hence that colimit is zero. Step 5 then gives $H^s(\widehat{\mathbf Z},M)=0$ for every torsion discrete $M$ and $s\geq2$. The current inflation statement explicitly uses source norm differential $N_n$ and target norm differential $eN_n$; its degree-$s$ map is multiplication by $e^{\lfloor s/2\rfloor}$ between those different complexes, and is zero because $eA=0$ and $s\geq2$.

source.place: Finite modules, inflation from level n to en; sk-lem-base-field-cd-inflation.proof.md, chain-map formula

proof.text: For every torsion étale sheaf $F$ on $\operatorname{Spec}K$, its stalk $M=E(F)$ is torsion: each germ is represented by a local section, and an integer killing that section kills its germ. Steps 1 and 4 identify $H^s(K_{\Et},F)$ with $H^s(\widehat{\mathbf Z},M)$, which step 7 shows is zero for $s\geq2$. In particular this holds for every $\ell$-power torsion étale sheaf. Applying part (2) of [det-cd-etale-comparison] on the qcqs scheme $\operatorname{Spec}K$, with auxiliary morphism $g=\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$, the supremum of degrees of nonzero cohomology is at most one. Thus $\operatorname{cd}_\ell(K)\leq1$, as required. No restriction on the characteristic or uniform exponent has entered this conclusion.

source.place: Consequences, finite-field torsion bound and étale/pro-étale comparison
